title: Pick from a list
prompt: Show the title and genre of books in History or Mystery. Replace the ___ with the list.
hints: List text values in single quotes, separated by commas.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre IN ('History', 'Mystery');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre IN ('History');
SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre NOT IN ('History', 'Mystery');

title: A price range
prompt: Show the title and price of books costing from 12 to 18.5, including both of those prices.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE price BETWEEN 12 AND 18.5;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE price > 12 AND price < 18.5;
SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE price BETWEEN 18.5 AND 12;
wrongSolutions.why: The lower value must come first

title: Not in the list
prompt: Show the name of employees whose id isn't 1, 2, or 3.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE employees SET id = 21 WHERE id = 1;

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id NOT IN (1, 2, 3);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3);
SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id NOT IN (1, 2);
wrongSolutions.why: Leaves out id 3 from the list

title: A week of dates
prompt: Show the city and reading_date of readings from 2024-03-02 to 2024-03-03, inclusive.
hints: BETWEEN works on dates written as YYYY-MM-DD.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE readings SET reading_date = '2024-03-03' WHERE id = 1; UPDATE readings SET reading_date = '2024-03-09' WHERE id = 2;

solutions: SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE reading_date BETWEEN '2024-03-02' AND '2024-03-03';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE reading_date > '2024-03-02' AND reading_date < '2024-03-03';
SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE reading_date = '2024-03-02';

title: Outside the range
prompt: Show the name and price of products that aren't priced from 4 to 25. Products priced exactly 4 or 25 should be left out.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price NOT BETWEEN 4 AND 25;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 4 AND 25;
SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price <= 4 OR price >= 25;

title: Fix the list
prompt: This should show customers from Pune or Tokyo, but it fails. Fix it.
hints: A list needs brackets and a comma between values.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city IN ('Pune', 'Tokyo');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city IN ('Pune');
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Pune';

title: Hired in a year, paid in a range
prompt: Show the name of employees hired during 2021 who earn from 48000 to 95000, inclusive.
hints: Use two BETWEENs joined with AND.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET hire_date = '2021-12-31', salary = 48000 WHERE id = 14; UPDATE employees SET hire_date = '2021-06-01', salary = 96000 WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE hire_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31' AND salary BETWEEN 48000 AND 95000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE hire_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31';
SELECT name FROM employees WHERE hire_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31' OR salary BETWEEN 48000 AND 95000;

title: A shortlist
prompt: Show the student_id and grade of enrolments in course 1 or 3 with a grade from 80 to 100.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 80, course_id = 1 WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT student_id, grade FROM enrolments WHERE course_id IN (1, 3) AND grade BETWEEN 80 AND 100;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id, grade FROM enrolments WHERE course_id IN (1, 3);
SELECT student_id, grade FROM enrolments WHERE course_id IN (1, 3) AND grade > 80;
wrongSolutions.why: Leaves out a grade of exactly 80
